page: Amazon Web Services c8a.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at 4.5 GHz with 1 thread per core. The cache structure consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core. Memory capacity is 96.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16), AVX VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance carries no local storage, contains no GPUs, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier execution across both single-threaded and parallel processing tasks. The AMD EPYC processor achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2818.0 and a multi-core score of 29814.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 102415.6. Stress-ng scores reflect similar compute density, measuring 3778.98 for single-core and 179310.02 for multi-core. Vector and compute-intensive operations perform strongly, including Geekbench software compilation with Clang at 79021.0 and ray tracing at 97708.0. Memory throughput reaches 10084.11 GB/sec for small cached reads and uncached reads of 291.31 GB/sec. In memory-bound operations, Redis achieved 154.22 million SET operations per second, while CPU-based LLM inference demonstrated high throughput, generating 54.99 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

Resource allocation focuses on raw computing density with a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Because local NVMe storage and GPUs are absent, workloads that require local scratch space or hardware acceleration are not well aligned. The high thread count, 4.5 GHz clock speed, AVX-512 capabilities, and fast DDR5 memory make this instance suitable for distributed build clusters, software compilation pipelines, batch compute jobs, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-concurrency microservices requiring consistent non-hyperthreaded processing power.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.12xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, utilizing dedicated 1:1 physical-to-virtual CPU mapping without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory (2.0 GB per core) and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 22 Gbps of baseline networking. Local storage and dedicated GPUs are absent. The platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded compute performance across benchmarks, including a PassMark CPU score of 102415.6, Geekbench multi-core score of 29814.0, and 154.22 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware includes AVX-512 vector acceleration, making it an efficient platform for distributed build pipelines, code compilation, CPU-bound scientific modeling, batch processing, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
